title_clean: Types of Traders in Stock Market
summary: Intro to derivatives-market participants: arbitrageurs, hedgers, speculators - the three groups that make up derivatives activity.
lessons: Derivatives participants fall into three functional groups: arbitrageurs, hedgers, speculators.
quotes: In derivatives there are lot of people and those people can be classified into three groups. One, arbitrageurs, two hedgers and three speculators.
enhance: Worked example of how the three participant types interact in one option trade

summary: Explains why Indian option symbols are PE/CE: they denote European-style put/call options, distinguishing exercise style from option type.
lessons: Indian option symbols PE/CE stand for European-style put/call - exercise style is embedded in the instrument naming.
quotes: PE stands for put option European style, CE stands for call option European style.
enhance: Table comparing American vs European exercise rights across NSE/BSE and US markets

title_clean: Money vs Experience in Stock Market
summary: Advises informed decisions over blind news-following; closes with the classic exchange between money and experience in markets.
lessons: Research before buying - do not follow news blindly; markets transfer money from the inexperienced to the experienced over time.
quotes: Stock market is the place where people with money meet people with experience, and after some time the people with experience become people with money.

title_clean: Don't Buy Gold in 2022 Before Watching This!
summary: Bearish 8-10 year gold thesis: Indian gold price = international price x USD/INR x tax. Stablecoins replaced gold as the crisis-hedge asset, so 2020 broke the historic crisis-spike pattern (1980, 2008).
lessons: Gold spikes only in genuine currency crises (1980 oil shock, 2008 Lehman); 2020 broke the pattern because stablecoins now do that hedging job.
Indian gold price has three drivers: international price, USD/INR rate, and local taxation (high tax breeds smuggling).
INR was stable 70-75 from 2013-2021 and was Asia's strongest currency 2014-2021; the 72-to-80 slide need not persist.
If no major fall happened, the market cannot rebound 100% - the rebound matches the depth of the fall.

event_claims.claim: Gold price was fixed by the UK government until roughly 1973-74, after which market forces set it; long-term charts start then
Gold spiked around the 1980 Iran oil crisis and after the 2008 Lehman collapse, but not during the 2020 COVID crash
Bank of America predicted gold would reach $3,000/oz during 2020; it did not
INR depreciated about 10% from 72 to 80 against USD in 2022 amid US inflation; USD/INR traded 70-75 from 2013-2021
India cut gold import tax a few months before Aug 2022 because high taxation fuels smuggling
Dubai was placed on FATF grey list over money-laundering controls, prompting stricter enforcement
During the Feb 2022 Russia-Ukraine war, capital flight from the region went into stablecoins rather than gold, capping gold demand

quotes: Until 2008, to hedge against currency depreciation there was only one thing available - gold. Now there is an alternate: crypto, stablecoin crypto.
The frog will never realize the heat keeps on increasing... people involved in a thing too deeply never realize change is happening.
enhance: Worked table: gold price in INR = international USD price x USD/INR x (1+tax), with 2011/2013/2020/2022 scenarios

summary: Humor segment: a joke about an American smoking a $100 note, a Russian a $1,000 note, and an Indian rolling a $1M cheque - showing off without spending.
Exercise-style difference: American options exercisable any day (early exercise complicates hedged positions); European options only at expiry or closed by trading.
lessons: American options can be exercised any day before expiry; European only at expiry - early-exercise risk is why hedgers must monitor assigned positions.
quotes: American options can be exercised at any point of time. That gives lot of trouble for people having hedged positions.
enhance: Early-assignment worked example: deep-ITM American call before ex-dividend

summary: Defines a derivative via the milk-curd-buttermilk-butter chain: something derived from an underlying, layered derivations.
lessons: A derivative is something derived from an underlying - like curd from milk, each layer's value derives from the prior one.
quotes: Derivative means something derived from the underlying - curd is a derivative of milk.

summary: Forward = bilateral contract, price fixed today for future execution; futures are the same but margin-traded and standardized. Student-vs-exporter USD example.
lessons: In a forward the price is decided today for future delivery; futures add standardization and daily settlement.
quotes: Forward: price will be decided today. Future is exactly the same, but the price is not decided today.
enhance: Side-by-side table: forward vs futures (counterparty risk, margining, standardization, settlement)

summary: Only two 100%+ post-bottom rallies in history: after Lehman 2008 and COVID 2020 - because the falls were 30-50%. No deep fall, no 100% rebound; ball-drop analogy.
lessons: 100% rallies followed only Lehman (2008) and COVID (2020) crashes - rebound magnitude reflects how deep the fall was.

event_claims.claim: Nifty rallied more than 100% from the bottom after both the 2008-09 Lehman crash and the 2020 COVID crash - the only such occasions

quotes: If you drop a ball from a very high place, when it touches the ground the rebounding is also very high.
enhance: Table: post-crash drawdown vs recovery magnitude/time for 2008 vs 2020

summary: Contrarian consumption philosophy: the 'invest instead of buying the bullet/biscuit' tweets miss the point - spending drives the economy; do not sacrifice today's happiness for tomorrow's.
lessons: Savings is overrated, spending underrated - spending is economic contribution; don't trade today's happiness for tomorrow's.
quotes: Savings is overrated, spending is underrated. Don't save for tomorrow's happiness by sacrificing today's happiness.
